skill.name: startup-business-analyst-market-opportunity
skill.description: Generate startup market opportunity analysis with TAM, SAM, SOM calculations, source research, and validation.
skill.summary: Guides defensible startup market sizing from context gathering through TAM, SAM, SOM, and investment thesis.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static command-execution and network-reconnaissance detections are false positives caused by Markdown formatting and business-analysis prose. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious workflow intent was found. The remaining concern is overbroad tool permissions because Bash is allowed without a clear need.

remediation.issue: Bash is allowed even though the skill workflow does not require shell execution.
remediation.suggestion: Remove Bash from allowed-tools and keep only the research and file tools needed for market analysis.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 27 contains a Markdown inline file reference, not a Ruby backtick expression or shell command. It instructs the agent to open a resource path and does not execute user-controlled input.
Lines 113-115 are a fenced Markdown formula for SAM calculation. The backticks delimit documentation and contain no executable command.
The matched range is Markdown documentation covering formulas and report sections. I found no shell invocation, Ruby interpolation, or instruction to execute the fenced text.
Line 187 uses inline code formatting for a suggested report filename. It is a static filename pattern, not command execution.
Lines 212-227 are a Markdown example conversation block. The content demonstrates expected dialogue and does not contain an executable shell command.
The finding is triggered by Markdown code fencing near an example block and subsequent command names. There is no shell syntax or dynamic execution path.
Line 232 formats a slash command name as inline code for documentation. It is not a shell command and does not execute anything.
Line 128 says "Go-to-market effectiveness" as a business factor for SOM estimation. This is not host discovery, scanning, or network reconnaissance.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Tool Permissions
semantic_findings.description: The front matter permits Bash along with research and file tools, but the instructions do not require shell execution. Unneeded shell access increases impact if later prompts misuse the skill.

content.value_statement: Market sizing is hard to defend when assumptions, sources, and methods are scattered. This skill guides TAM, SAM, and SOM analysis with sourced calculations and validation.
actual_capabilities: Collects product, customer, pricing, stage, and geography context.
Guides bottom-up TAM calculations for SaaS, consumer, marketplace, and commerce models.
Uses web research to find industry reports, filings, public data, and trade sources.
Validates TAM with top-down market estimates and explains major variance.
Narrows TAM into SAM with geography, product fit, readiness, and switching filters.
Projects SOM with conservative three-year and five-year market share assumptions.
limitations: It depends on source quality and does not guarantee complete market data.
It does not replace professional investment, legal, or financial advice.
It creates narrative analysis, not a full spreadsheet model.
The referenced implementation playbook is not included in this package.

use_cases.title: Validate a Seed Pitch Market
use_cases.description: Build defensible TAM, SAM, and SOM numbers before adding them to an investor deck.

use_cases.title: Compare Expansion Segments
use_cases.description: Estimate opportunity size across customer segments, geographies, or pricing models before prioritizing a roadmap.

use_cases.title: Review Venture-Scale Potential
use_cases.description: Create a structured market opportunity memo with sources, assumptions, risks, and sanity checks.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Market Size
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with known product and customer basics.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to analyze market opportunity for a startup. Product: [product]. Target customers: [customers]. Pricing model: [pricing]. Geography: [region]. Stage: [stage].

prompt_templates.title: Build TAM, SAM, and SOM
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a full sizing workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a TAM, SAM, and SOM analysis for [startup idea]. Use bottom-up sizing first, validate with top-down sources, and document every assumption.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Customer Segments
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze market opportunity across these segments: [segment list]. Estimate segment size, ACV or ARPU, adoption readiness, competition, and likely obtainable share.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Investor-Ready Memo
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a sourced report and investment thesis.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare an investor-ready market opportunity memo for [company]. Include sourced market data, bottom-up and top-down calculations, SAM filters, SOM projection, public-company benchmarks, risks, and next steps.

output_examples.input: A B2B SaaS startup sells compliance automation to mid-market health care providers in the United States.
output_examples.output: A market sizing report with target segments, source-backed company counts, ACV assumptions, TAM and SAM calculations, SOM projections, and investment risks.

output_examples.input: A consumer marketplace wants to size North American demand before raising a seed round.
output_examples.output: A founder-ready summary that estimates addressable users, transaction frequency, take rate, geographic filters, realistic share capture, and validation gaps.

output_examples.input: A product team needs to choose between enterprise, mid-market, and small business expansion.
output_examples.output: A segment comparison that ranks opportunity by revenue potential, readiness, competition, reachability, and fit with current product capabilities.

best_practices: Provide pricing, customer segment, geography, and stage before requesting calculations.
Ask for source dates and assumption notes beside every major estimate.
Use conservative SOM assumptions unless strong evidence supports higher share.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on one top-down market report as the only sizing method.
Do not mix consumer, buyer, and revenue units in the same calculation.
Do not present optimistic SOM without competition and go-to-market constraints.

faq.question: What inputs should I prepare first?
faq.answer: Prepare the product description, customer profile, pricing model, company stage, and initial geography.

faq.question: Can it research market data?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill instructs the agent to use web research and cite sources with URLs and dates.

faq.question: Does it support B2B and consumer models?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes frameworks for B2B SaaS, consumer products, marketplaces, transactions, and commerce models.

faq.question: How does it validate TAM?
faq.answer: It compares bottom-up calculations with top-down market estimates and explains large differences.

faq.question: Will it create a final report?
faq.answer: Yes. It can produce a Markdown report with executive summary, calculations, validation, risks, and next steps.

faq.question: Is the output investment advice?
faq.answer: No. It is structured research support and should be reviewed before business or investment decisions.
